headline: High: Devin’s broad workspace and write privileges can collide with open-webui’s persistent, tool-rich sessions, creating dangerous shared-state, prompt-injection, and data-leak pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, while open-webui supports MCP, plugins, and persistent sessions. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if Devin ingests open-webui output or shared artifacts as trusted content. The pair is not proven to share a channel by default, so this is medium, not high.
conditions: IF Devin reads open-webui-generated text from a shared workspace, chat, or MCP tool output as instructions, injection becomes actionable.
IF open-webui exposes attacker-controlled content through a plugin or tool response that Devin parses, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of open-webui outputs into Devin prompts.
Require explicit human review before Devin acts on any open-webui-generated instructions.
Restrict shared MCP/tool channels to allowlisted schemas only.
Add provenance tags to all cross-agent artifacts.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate workspaces with no shared message bus.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo clones, cloud workspace files, and secrets such as deploy keys and integration tokens; open-webui touches local/mounted files, API keys, and persistent memory. If they share files or a mounted volume, sensitive data can flow from Devin into open-webui’s broader tool ecosystem and external APIs. The pairwise leakage pathway is credible and the blast radius includes secrets.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or mounted volume, secrets and documents can be exposed across the pair.
IF open-webui forwards file contents or memory to an external model/API, Devin-held secrets can leave the workspace.
mitigations: Remove shared filesystem access between the agents.
Store secrets only in per-agent secret stores, not files.
Disable file-upload and memory-sync features in open-webui for shared projects.
Rotate any tokens that may have been present in shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and egress filtering.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted cloud-workspace shell, filesystem write, and git mutation; open-webui can access mounted files and run tools/plugins with broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or volume, concurrent writes and git state changes can race and corrupt work. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces, so the conflict is real in default collaborative setups.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or mounted directory, file-level conflicts can occur.
IF both agents modify git state without external locking, commits and branches can diverge or be overwritten.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Use a single-writer policy for git operations.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Add lock files or a queue around mutable resources.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously produce code, docs, and task updates, while open-webui can route tool outputs through plugins and persistent memory. If open-webui treats Devin’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or stored memory. The pair does not inherently force blind trust, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF open-webui stores Devin output in persistent memory without verification, later responses can amplify errors.
IF open-webui triggers tools based on Devin-generated text, incorrect facts can become actions.
mitigations: Require citation or schema checks before accepting Devin output.
Mark Devin output as untrusted in open-webui memory.
Add a human approval step before tool execution.
Limit open-webui automation on content originating from Devin.
requires-engineering: implement validation gates for cross-agent handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin is documented handling team chat, issue trackers, docs, and integration tokens in a vendor-managed cloud workspace; open-webui handles prompts, chat messages, files, notes, and API keys with persistent sessions. If regulated or sensitive data is routed between them, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is shared across both agents, their differing storage and retention behaviors can create policy mismatch.
IF open-webui persists prompts or files longer than Devin’s workspace retention, deletion/export obligations may fail.
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent.
Disable persistence for regulated projects in open-webui.
Keep sensitive work out of shared sessions.
Review retention settings on both systems.
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows across the pair.
